title: Method to Evaluate Microbial Degradation Activity in Silage and Manure
author: Nikolić, Massaro, et al.

steps.title: Obtain and cut threads
steps.instruction: Purchase cotton thread n° 16 and silk thread “Bozzolo Reale” n° 24 from Cucirini Tre Stelle s.r.l. (Milan, Italy) and cut each filament to a length of 10 cm.

steps.title: Prepare nylon bags
steps.instruction: Use woven nylon bags (Ankom, 50 ± 10 µm porosity, 5 cm × 5 cm) and sew the top edge to keep contents inside.

steps.title: Load threads into bags
steps.instruction: Place six 10‑cm cotton threads in one bag and six 10‑cm silk threads in another bag. For each trial prepare two bags per thread type (total 12 cotton and 12 silk measurements).

steps.title: Set up experimental trials
steps.instruction: Insert the sealed bags into the chosen microbial environment (silage, rumen fluid, manure or slurry) and incubate for the required period (e.g., 12, 24 or 48 h) as defined by the experimental design.

steps.title: Retrieve and dry threads
steps.instruction: After incubation, remove the bags, open them, extract the threads and allow them to air‑dry until completely dry.

steps.title: Attach threads to keyring
steps.instruction: Pinch the end of each dried thread and coil it several times around a keyring to secure it for testing.

steps.title: Measure breaking force
steps.instruction: Set the digital dynamometer (IMADA ZP, ELIS Electronic Instruments and Systems, Rome, Italy) to the “peak” function mode. Pull each thread attached to the keyring until it breaks and record the peak force value.

steps.title: Measure untreated standards
steps.instruction: Measure the rupture force of non‑treated (new) cotton and silk threads under the same conditions to obtain standard values (Rni).

steps.title: Calculate resistance percentage
steps.instruction: Compute resistance R for each treated thread using the formula R = (Ri / Rni) × 100, where Ri is the rupture value of the incubated thread and Rni is the rupture value of the untreated thread.

steps.title: Convert to degradation percentage
steps.instruction: Calculate degradation D as D = 100 – R.

steps.title: Statistical analysis – ANOVA
steps.instruction: Perform factorial ANOVA on the degradation data after Levene’s test, followed by Tukey post‑hoc test, using the R environment.

steps.title: Estimate variance components
steps.instruction: Using PROC MIXED (SAS 2005), fit separate mixed linear models for: (a) silage degradability (random effects: silage type S, repetition R1, interaction S×R1, error e1); (b) rumen fluid degradability at 12, 24, 48 h (random effects: rumen fluid RF, repetition R2, interaction RF×R2, error e2); (c) waste (manure or slurry) degradability (random effects: repetition R3, error e3). Apply the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) method.

steps.title: Compute repeatability metrics
steps.instruction: For each model calculate: RT = 2√2 σe, CV = (RT × Mean × 100)⁻¹, RT% = (σ²_random / (σ²_random + σe²)) × 100, using the formulas provided for silage, rumen fluid, and waste trials.
